items.title: fix(request): keep the body readable when form data parsing fails
items.body:
Fixes #5383

### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code
- [ ] Add [TSDoc](https://tsdoc.org/)/[JSDoc](https://jsdoc.app/about-getting-started) to document the code

### What was wrong

`c.req.formData()` keeps only the parsed result and throws the body away. If the body isn't a form, that result is a rejected promise — and it stays in the cache, so every other way of reading the same body gets handed the same rejection:

```ts
app.post('/', async (c) => {
  try {
    await c.req.formData() // JSON body, so this throws
  } catch {}

  const body = await c.req.json() // throws too
})
```

`text()`, `json()`, `arrayBuffer()`, `bytes()` and `blob()` all fail after that.

Node makes it worse than it looks: `raw.formData()` consumes the stream even when it rejects (undici marks the body as used before it checks the media type), so there is nothing left to read afterwards — `raw.text()` throws `Body is unusable`. The bytes have to be read *before* the parse, not after.

### The fix

`c.req.parseBody()` already gets this right: it reads the bytes first and parses them afterwards, so a failed parse leaves the body readable. This makes `formData()` follow the same order, reusing `bufferToFormData()` — which is still the runtime's own parser, just fed from the cached bytes instead of the live stream:

```ts
if (key === 'formData') {
  return (bodyCache.formData = this.arrayBuffer().then((buffer) =>
    bufferToFormData(buffer, raw.headers.get('content-type') ?? '').then((formData) => {
      // ...
      return formData
    })
  ))
}
```

### Keeping `bodyCache` the shape callers expect

`cloneRawRequest()` and the cache middleware both read `Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]` and expect `formData` there once a form has been parsed:

- `src/request.ts` — `cloneRawRequest()`
- `src/middleware/cache/index.ts`

So the original order is restored **only when the parse succeeds**. After a failure the raw bytes stay first, which is exactly what makes the other representations readable again. Both of those callers keep working with no changes.

### Tests

Added to `src/request.test.ts`, next to the existing `should not break body methods after parseBody() with non-form content-type`:

- `text()` / `json()` / `arrayBuffer()` / `bytes()` / `blob()`, each after a failed `formData()`
- a second `formData()` still reports the parse failure
- trying another representation after a failed parse (the `try`/`catch` fallback)

Six of the seven fail without the change and pass with it.

- `vitest --run src/request.test.ts src/middleware/cache/index.test.ts src/utils/body.test.ts` — 253 passed
- full suite — 5141 passed, 44 skipped. The 12 failures in `color` / `logger` / `dev` / `compress(node)` are colour- and TTY-dependent and fail the same way on an unmodified checkout
- `tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit` — clean
- `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` — no further changes

### Out of scope

After a *successful* `formData()`, `text()` still returns the re-serialized form instead of the original bytes. Same root cause, different trigger — fixing it would change the cache shape on the success path too, and with it the two callers above, so it belongs in its own change.
